text:
maria: Hey infra team — can we iterate on a Grafana dashboard for the GPU fleet? Need panels for utilization, memory used vs capacity, temps/thermals, and power draw. Also want templating by region/pool and low-noise alerts.

sam: +1. I'll sketch panels: overall cluster utilization, per-GPU utilization, memory usage percent, power (W), temperature (C), and a thermal throttling indicator.

jake: For metrics we should use dcgm exporters + node-exporter for chassis temps. Example promql for GPU util:
```
avg by (gpu_id) (dcgm_gpu_sm_utilization{env="prod"})
```
and memory used percent: 
```
(dcgm_gpu_mem_used_bytes / dcgm_gpu_mem_total_bytes) * 100
```

olivia: Important: support MIG and non-MIG GPUs. For MIG, group by `gpu_instance` label; for normal GPUs use `gpu_id`. Also add a template variable `$pool` that filters `cluster_pool=~"$pool"`.

maria: Good call on MIG. Can we also add a panel for per-node aggregate (sum of GPUs on node) so SREs can quickly see noisy neighbors?

sam: Yep. Node-level query (per node):
```
sum by (node) (dcgm_gpu_sm_utilization{env="prod", cluster_pool=~"$pool"}) / count by (node) (dcgm_gpu_sm_utilization{env="prod", cluster_pool=~"$pool"})
```
That gives avg GPU util per node.

jake: For thermals add a heatmap or table of `dcgm_gpu_temp` and include annotations for thermal throttling events from our logs (Loki). We can show spikes alongside pod deploy annotations.

olivia: Dashboard provisioning: put JSON at `grafana/dashboards/gpu/gpu-fleet.json` in infra-monitoring repo, UID `gpu-fleet-v1`. Keep version in the file and reference via provisioning folder. I'll open a PR.

maria: Alerting: avoid noise. Suggested alerts:
- GPU temp > 90C sustained for 2m -> warn
- GPU temp > 95C for 30s -> critical
- Power draw > expected by 20% for 5m (possible runaway) -> warn
- Overall cluster GPU capacity usage > 85% for 15m -> page (but only for prod pools)

kevin: Re: capacity alert, we should tie to an SLO for 'capacity availability' — e.g., 99.9% of time >= X free GPUs per pool. We can compute free by: total GPUs - sum(allocated_gpus). Might be noisy; use 5m rollout window.

jake: For alert queries, use recording rules where possible so dashboards and alerts reference stable names. Example recording rule: `gpu:utilization:avg5m` -> avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_sm_utilization[5m]). Alerts can then check `gpu:utilization:avg5m > 85`.

sam: UX details: default to last 6h, have a dropdown for `region`, `pool`, `gpu_model`. Add panel links to node pages and a runbook link. Keep large panels for per-node table with sort by hottest/power draw.

olivia: I'll add annotations for deploys and outageINC incidents. Also add a small panel that shows the exporter's scrape health (dcgm_exporter up metric) and last seen timestamp so oncall can quickly tell if missing metrics vs real issues.

maria: Can we include a 'cost' panel showing power $/hr estimate? use `dcgm_gpu_power_draw_watts` and multiply by `region_energy_price` from a dashboard constant, then display an estimated hourly cost. Not for billing accuracy, but helpful for ops decisions.

kevin: Love the cost idea. We should also tag the dashboards with `sla-class` label (prod/staging) so dashboards and alerts use different thresholds.

infra-bot: grafana-provisioner: created dashboard skeleton at `grafana/dashboards/gpu/gpu-fleet.json` (UID=c1f2g3h4). Commit: https://git.redwood/infra-monitoring/commit/abcd1234

sam: I'll iterate on panel layouts tonight. Plan: 1) Cluster overview row, 2) Node table row, 3) Thermal/power row, 4) MIG-specific row, 5) Alert/health row, 6) Cost & runbooks.

maria: Thanks. Last ask: please add a small guide in the dashboard README explaining alert rationale and how to tune thresholds per pool (example: training pools tolerate higher sustained util than realtime pools).

olivia: Will do. I'll tag the PR with `monitoring` and `gpu-fleet` and link to the runbook draft.

maria: Sweet. @kevin can you review the SLO math once PR is up?

kevin: Yep, ping me after PR. Also let's add a Grafana annotation for when autoscaler did a scale up/scale down event — helps correlate utilization spikes to scaler behavior.

jake: One more thing: add a compact sparkline column in the node table (last 1h) so you can eyeball trending without opening the node page. Use `sparklines` with `gpu:utilization:avg1h` recording rule.

sam: Great notes. I'll upload the first draft and assign reviewers. Expect PR link in ~2-3 hours. :hourglass: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
